setup_summary.text: Caterpillar reports fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-01-27 before the open. Consensus is EPS $7.08 and revenue $21.65B. Whisper EPS and an options-implied move are not yet available. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±4.7%.

Q3 2026 (reported Oct 29) was another strong quarter. Sales and revenues were $20.682B (+17% y/y), adjusted EPS was $7.20 (vs $4.95) and adjusted operating margin was 20.6% (vs 17.5%). Volume added $2.2B and price $663M, and all three primary segments grew.

Q3 beat consensus: revenue was above the $20.55B LSEG consensus and adjusted EPS was about 2.4% above. The stock still fell about 3.8% to $622.75 on the print, and is roughly 38% below its June 30 high. The reaction centred on the unchanged full-year growth target and backlog concerns.

The Q3 operating profit of $4.214B included $128M of IEEPA tariff recoveries, nearly all booked in corporate items. Removing them from adjusted operating profit of $4.255B leaves about $4.13B, or roughly 20.0% of sales (derived). Year-to-date recoveries are about $520M, and none are assumed in Q4.

Backlog is a record of about $78B, up about $38B (96%) y/y and about $6B from $72.1B at June 30 (derived). It has grown for four straight quarters in all three primary segments. About 58% is expected to ship within 12 months (59% last quarter). Large reciprocating engine orders are being taken into 2029 and turbine orders into 2030.

Q4 is a base-effect and mix quarter. Management guides 'moderate' sales growth against a strong Q4 2025. Construction Industries sales should be about flat y/y, with a roughly $1.6B seasonal dealer-inventory drawdown (vs $600M last year, about a $1B volume headwind). Power & Energy should grow moderately and Resource Industries strongly. Enterprise adjusted operating margin is guided higher y/y.

Sales to users stayed strong in Q3: total +22% (Q2 +25%). Power Generation was +75%, Construction Industries +20% (North America +27%) and Resource Industries only +4% (rail -70%). The data comes from voluntary, unaudited dealer reports.

Capital return continues. Q3 deployed $1.2B to buybacks and about $0.7B to dividends. Nine-month buybacks were $7.745B and dividends $2.148B. The quarterly dividend was raised 8% to $1.63 in June. Enterprise cash was $7.9B at September 30 (vs $10.0B at year-end), and inventories rose to $22.2B (from $18.1B).

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 sales and revenues were $20.682B (+17% y/y); nine-month revenue was $58.640B vs $48.456B.

consensus.text: Consensus is $21.65B. Against the correct Q4 2025 base (about $19.13B, derived from FY2025 $67.589B less nine-month $48.456B) this is about +13% y/y and +4.7% sequentially. The XBRL-derived +22.7% uses the Q3 2025 base and should be ignored.

view.text: Consensus sits at the top of what guidance supports. $21.65B would make FY2026 about $80.3B, or +18.8%, the high end of 'mid-to-high teens'. Flat sequential sales would give about +17.4%. Management guided Q4 only 'moderate', with Construction Industries flat and a ~$1B dealer-destock volume headwind. A plausible range is roughly $20.9B-$21.7B, with modest downside risk to the consensus point.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $7.20 (GAAP $7.13), including $128M of IEEPA recoveries. That is worth about $0.21/share after a 23% tax rate on about 461M diluted shares (derived), so ex-recoveries it was about $6.99.

consensus.text: Consensus is $7.08, roughly +38% y/y against a Q4 2025 adjusted EPS of about $5.14 (FY2025 adjusted $19.06 less H1 $8.97 and Q3 $4.95, derived). The XBRL-derived +45.1% uses the Q3 base. A $7.12 figure in a 10/23 article was a pre-Q3 consensus, not Q4.

view.text: $7.08 is about 1% above Q3 ex-recoveries ($6.99) on roughly 5% higher sales, with no IEEPA help and a larger-than-usual Construction Industries margin step-down. That looks achievable but not conservative. Upside needs price/volume to beat and freight and capacity costs to stay contained.

last_reported.text: Q3 adjusted operating margin was 20.6% (about 20.0% excluding $128M of recoveries, derived). Q4 2025 adjusted was about 15.6% (FY2025 adjusted operating profit $11.595B less H1 $5.527B and Q3 $3.089B, over about $19.13B of sales, derived).

view.text: Management guides a higher margin y/y, helped by price, volume and tariffs about $200M lower than Q4 2025. Headwinds are freight, capacity-expansion costs including depreciation, higher SG&A/R&D and a larger-than-typical Construction Industries step-down. Full-year ex-recoveries margin is guided 'near the bottom' of the target range, whose bounds are not quantified in the sources. My rough read of consensus EPS implies a margin of about 19-20% (assumes 23% tax, 461M shares and other income roughly equal to interest expense).

metrics_to_model.metric: Construction Industries dealer inventory change and segment margin

last_reported.text: Q3 Construction Industries dealer inventory rose $300M (vs +$600M in Q3 2025). Q3 segment sales were $7.983B and profit $1.831B (22.9% margin vs 20.4%).

view.text: Guided Q4 drawdown is about $1.6B vs $600M a year ago, a ~$1B volume headwind, so sales are guided about flat and volume 'down modestly'. Year-end dealer inventory should still be about $700M above year-end 2025. Price stays favorable and margin should rise y/y but step down from Q3 by slightly more than usual.

metrics_to_model.metric: Power & Energy sales and segment margin

last_reported.text: Q3 Power & Energy sales were $8.784B (+18%) and segment profit $2.143B (+31%, 24.4% margin vs 21.9%). Power Generation external sales were $3.421B (+30%), Oil & Gas $2.236B (+13%), Industrial $1.631B (+4%).

view.text: Guide is moderate sales growth against a strong prior-year quarter, limited by capacity ('no slack', a test cell went down in Q3). Margin is expected higher y/y and similar to Q3's 24.4%, with price and volume offset by depreciation, expansion expense, freight and materials. First 10-megawatt MaK units ship in Q4.

metrics_to_model.metric: Resource Industries sales, sales to users and margin

last_reported.text: Q3 Resource Industries sales were $4.615B (+15%) and profit $622M (13.5% margin vs 13.6%). Sales to users rose only 4% (mining +8%, rail -70%), below management's expectations on shipping and commissioning delays.

view.text: Management expects commissioning delays to catch up and strong Q4 sales growth, with a higher margin y/y on price and volume, partly offset by freight and material costs. The key check is whether the catch-up arrives and whether the mining-truck ramp inefficiencies ease. Locomotive deliveries are now seen slightly lower for the year.

last_reported.text: Backlog was a record of about $78B at September 30 (up $38B y/y), vs $72.1B at June 30 and $51.2B at year-end 2025.

view.text: Management says backlog will be lumpy, as big prime-power and mining orders land unevenly, and that book-to-bill (an analyst put it at about 1.3, down from about 1.7) moves with rising production. A smaller sequential increase, or a flat reading, would be consistent with the call but could feed the 'backlog doubts' that hit the stock.

last_reported.text: Q3 tariff costs were about $600M excluding IEEPA, roughly flat y/y. Year-to-date IEEPA recoveries are about $520M ($392M in Q2, $128M in Q3).

view.text: Q4 tariff costs are guided at about $600M, about $200M below Q4 2025, and full-year about $2.2B (the February view was about $2.6B). No further IEEPA recoveries are in the outlook, so any additional recovery would be upside to reported margin. Remaining claims were 'not probable' at June 30.

metrics_to_model.metric: Cat Financial credit: provision and allowance

last_reported.text: Q3 past dues were 1.31% (vs 1.47% a year ago), net write-offs $28M (vs $40M) and the allowance $332M, or 0.91% of finance receivables (0.84% at June 30). Segment profit rose 10% to $264M despite a $34M higher provision.

view.text: Credit quality is benign (past dues the lowest since 1998), but the allowance rate and provision have stepped up as the portfolio grows. Watch whether the allowance rate keeps rising and whether the provision drag persists.

metrics_to_model.metric: MP&E free cash flow, capex and restructuring

last_reported.text: H1 MP&E free cash flow was $5.698B and Q3 was $3.8B, about $9.5B through nine months (derived). H1 restructuring was $243M and Q3 $41M. Q3 MP&E capex was about $700M.

view.text: Guidance: MP&E free cash flow in the top half of the $6B-$15B range, capex about $3.3B (from about $3.5B) and restructuring about $300M. That implies only about $15-20M of restructuring in Q4 (derived) and roughly $1.3B of Q4 MP&E capex (derived), a step-up from Q3's $0.7B. Large customer advances ($5.3B) and the inventory build are the working-capital swing factors.

last_reported.text: Q3 other income was $135M (vs $208M), hurt by total return swap impacts. Q3 diluted shares were 460.9M vs 470.8M a year earlier.

view.text: Other income is volatile: total return swap and deferred-compensation fair-value moves flow through other income and corporate costs. The tax rate is guided at about 23%. Buybacks added about $0.15 to Q3 adjusted EPS y/y.

claim.text: Management continues to expect mid-to-high-teens sales and revenue growth (same as the 10-Q). Nine-month growth is about 21%, and analysts model about 18%.

guidance.guidance: Moderate y/y growth against a tough comparison; Power & Energy moderate, Construction Industries about flat, Resource Industries strong

claim.text: Q4 guide: moderate sales growth y/y against a strong Q4 2025. Power & Energy moderate, Construction Industries about flat (volume down modestly, price favorable) and Resource Industries strong.

guidance.guidance: Seasonal drawdown of about $1.6B (vs $600M in Q4 2025), about a $1B volume headwind; year-end inventory still above year-end 2025

claim.text: The 10-Q said only a decrease of 'over $1.0B'. The call quantifies about $1.6B and says year-end dealer inventory should still be higher than a year earlier, by almost $700M.

guidance.guidance: Full year near the bottom of the target range excluding IEEPA recoveries but higher than 2025; Q4 higher y/y; aim for the midpoint over time

claim.text: Management reiterates a full-year margin near the bottom of the target range ex-IEEPA and a higher Q4 margin y/y. It expects to 'claw off the bottom' from 2027, with more detail in January. The range bounds are not quantified in the sources.

guidance.guidance: About $2.2B for the year; about $600M in Q4 (about $200M below Q4 2025); split about 50% CI / 25% P&E / 25% RI; no further IEEPA recoveries assumed

claim.text: The full-year $2.2B was unchanged vs the 10-Q (February guide was about $2.6B). The Q4 figure of about $600M is new.
Lowered from about $3.5B in the 10-Q and 10-K, even as capacity expansions (Winston-Salem, a $1B Sanford investment) are announced.
Now at the low end of the prior $300-350M range. Through nine months about $284M has been incurred (derived from $243M in H1 and $41M in Q3).
The estimated annual rate is unchanged at about 23%.

guidance.guidance: Top half of the $6B-$15B annual target range

claim.text: Maintained on the call. The range itself is not in the 10-Q or 10-K, so it cannot be verified against the filings.

guidance.guidance: Now slightly lower y/y on delivery timing; rail services still expected to grow

claim.text: The 10-Q (Aug 5) said both locomotive deliveries and rail services were anticipated to grow. The call (Oct 29, newer) now expects deliveries slightly lower. Q3 rail sales fell 5% and rail retail fell 70%.

since_filing.text: Q3 results (Oct 29) are the main change since the Q2 10-Q (Aug 5). Sales and revenues were $20.682B (+17%), adjusted EPS $7.20 and backlog about $78B. The CFO said sales, operating profit and segment results were in line with management's expectations, apart from Resource Industries sales to users, which were below.

Contradiction on Resource Industries volume: the 10-Q (Aug 5) expected Q3 volume to be driven by higher sales of equipment to end users, but the call (Oct 29, newer) said sales to users rose only 4%, 'below our expectations', on mining shipping and commissioning delays. Reported sales were still +15% with volume +$478M and profit +14%.

Contradiction on Resource Industries pricing: the 10-Q guided Q3 price realization 'to a lesser extent' than Q2's. The release (newer) shows +$96M vs Q2's +$75M, and the CFO called it slightly better than expected on positive geographic mix.

Contradiction on Asia/Pacific: the 10-Q said 'softer economic conditions' outside China, while the call (newer) says 'stable'. Q3 Asia/Pacific Construction Industries sales to users were still down 2% and sales up only 2%, with some Latin America and Asia/Pacific ex-China weakness vs management's expectations.

IEEPA recoveries continued. The 10-Q booked $392M in Q2 and said further amounts were not probable. Q3 added $128M, taking the year-to-date total to about $520M. The outlook excludes more. The company's total IEEPA tariff cost was about $1.0B.
Leadership: Derrick York succeeds Denise Johnson as Resource Industries group president, and the company said Johnson will retire. This lands as the segment works through operational ramp issues.

Sell-side reaction: Oppenheimer reiterated Outperform with a $1,009 target after Q3, and Citigroup kept Buy with a target cut to $950. Baird kept Neutral and cut its target to a reported $729, which looks inconsistent with the other targets and needs verification.

Peer read-across (proxy): Komatsu raised its projected sales and profits for the fiscal year ending March 2027, citing stronger-than-expected demand across many regions in construction, mining and utility equipment and a greater-than-expected yen depreciation. Its first-half operating profit rose 3.5%, helped by yen depreciation, better selling prices and volume, but July-September operating profit fell 1.2%. Deere's Construction & Forestry sales (quarter ended Aug 2) grew 18% with +8 pts of price realization, and Deere reported a $502M direct tariff impact in the first nine months of 2026, net of tariff recovery.

key_debates.question: Is the $21.65B Q4 revenue consensus consistent with management's 'moderate growth' guide?

bull.text: Backlog is a record $78B, orders are strong across all three primary segments, and sales to users rose 22% in Q3. Management says capacity is ramping and expects favorable price realization in Q4. The $1.6B Construction Industries dealer-inventory drawdown still leaves year-end inventory almost $700M higher than a year earlier.

bear.text: The guide is 'moderate' growth on a tough comp, with Construction Industries flat, a ~$1B dealer-destock volume headwind, Power & Energy capacity-paced and Resource Industries still ramping. Consensus implies +4.7% sequentially and FY +18.8%, the top of the guide, and the usual Q4 step-up is 5-10% per an analyst.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 sales and revenues vs $21.65B, Construction Industries volume and dealer inventory change, and Power & Energy shipments vs capacity.

key_debates.question: Can margins move off the bottom of the target range in Q4 and 2027?

bull.text: Price realization is running at +$663M, tariffs are about $200M lower y/y in Q4, volume is leveraging, and margins rose 310bp y/y in Q3. Management expects to claw off the bottom and work back to the midpoint over a couple of years.

bear.text: Manufacturing costs were unfavorable in all three primary segments in Q3: freight, material costs (including tariffs) and capacity-expansion depreciation. Q3 adjusted operating margin of 20.6% included $128M of IEEPA recoveries, and full-year margin ex-IEEPA is guided near the bottom of the target range. Resource Industries segment margin was roughly flat (13.5% vs 13.6%). Management also expects higher SG&A/R&D and flags higher freight costs from elevated energy prices.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 adjusted operating margin ex-IEEPA vs the guided y/y increase, segment manufacturing-cost bridges, and the January 2027 margin commentary.

key_debates.question: How durable is the record backlog and data-center-driven Power & Energy demand?

bull.text: Orders run into 2029-2030 for large engines and turbines, frame agreements sit beyond the backlog, prime-power quoting is rising, and management sees no significant change in customer timing, permitting or credit. Power Generation sales to users were +75%.

bear.text: Book-to-bill has slowed from about 1.7 to about 1.3 (analyst figure), large orders are lumpy, management declined to quantify hyperscaler share, and analysts raised credit and permitting counterparty risk. The stock fell on 'backlog doubts' despite the beat.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 backlog and book-to-bill, any change in lead-time or delivery-slot language, and management's answer on customer mix.

key_debates.question: Will Resource Industries recover from the Q3 shortfall?

bull.text: Three straight quarters of strong orders (copper, gold, oil sands), commissioning delays are expected to catch up in Q4, and price is favorable. Management calls the ramp issues 'normal growing pains'.

bear.text: Q3 sales to users rose only 4%, rail sales to users fell 70%, locomotive deliveries were cut, margin was flat at 13.5% on tariff and material costs and H1 segment profit was down 10%. A leadership change is under way.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Resource Industries sales to users, segment margin vs 13.5% in Q3, and the pace of large mining truck output.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Revenue lands near or above $21.7B as Power & Energy output and Resource Industries catch-up beat the 'moderate' guide. Adjusted EPS is above $7.08, margins step up and backlog grows again, with FY revenue growth near the high end of the mid-to-high teens and a constructive 2027 outline.

triggers: Resource Industries commissioning delays reverse and sales to users are strong
Power & Energy shipments rise sequentially despite the capacity limit
Freight and capacity costs stay contained, tariffs about $600M
Backlog rises again and management signals margin improvement in 2027

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Q4 lands in line with management's guide of moderate sales growth y/y, against consensus of $21.65B revenue and $7.08 EPS. Adjusted operating margin is higher y/y, but the larger-than-usual Construction Industries Q4 margin step-down and freight and cost inflation keep full-year margin ex-IEEPA near the bottom of the target range, with full-year sales growth in the mid- to high teens.

triggers: Construction Industries dealer inventory falls about $1.6B as guided
Q4 tariffs about $600M with no further IEEPA recoveries
Backlog flat to modestly higher; the 2027 detail is deferred to the call

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue falls short of $21.65B on capacity hiccups, a deeper dealer destock or Resource Industries delays. Freight, depreciation and SG&A pressure margins, and adjusted EPS misses $7.08. A softer backlog or book-to-bill reading revives the 'backlog doubts', and the stock moves more than the ±4.7% average.

triggers: Another production disruption in Power & Energy (e.g. test-cell issues)
Resource Industries ramp problems persist and rail stays weak
Freight and material cost inflation exceeds plan
Backlog flat or down sequentially, or order timing slips

claim.text: Capacity is the pacing factor in Power & Energy ('hand to mouth', 'no slack', a Q3 test-cell outage). A production disruption would hit shipments and margins directly. Resource Industries is also working through ramp inefficiencies on large mining trucks.

Cost inflation: higher freight from elevated energy prices, capacity-expansion expense including depreciation, and tariffs weighed on Q3 manufacturing costs in all three primary segments. Higher SG&A/R&D is also expected.

Dealer inventory and Construction Industries timing: a ~$1.6B Q4 destock (vs $600M last year) is a ~$1B volume headwind, and rental fleet loading (Major Projects JV) contributes less in Q4. Dealers are independent, so the destock could be larger or smaller than guided.

Data-center and order-quality risk: backlog extends to 2029-2030, orders are lumpy, hyperscaler share is undisclosed and analysts raised credit and permitting counterparty concerns. A slowdown in orders or deferred slots would undercut the growth narrative.

Trade policy and IEEPA: tariffs of about $2.2B are guided for 2026. Remaining IEEPA refund claims are uncertain in timing and amount and not assumed in guidance, and a large import-overpayment receivable sat on the balance sheet at June 30. Reported margins carry $520M of non-recurring recoveries year-to-date.
Cat Financial credit: past dues are low, but the allowance rose to 0.91% and the Q3 provision increased $34M. The 10-K lists credit losses at Cat Financial as a key exposure.
Leadership transition in Resource Industries (Derrick York succeeds Denise Johnson) coincides with the segment's ramp challenges and rail weakness.

questions_for_management.question: Your full-year guide and consensus imply Q4 sales only about 1-5% above Q3. What explains the limited sequential growth beyond the destock and the comp: capacity, supplier constraints, or shipment timing in Power & Energy and Resource Industries?

why.text: An analyst noted that the full-year guide implies Q4 revenue is barely up sequentially, versus a typical 5-10% Q4 step-up.

questions_for_management.question: Please bridge Q4 adjusted operating margin ex-IEEPA vs Q3 (about 20.0%): how much do freight, capacity depreciation, SG&A/R&D and the Construction Industries step-down each take?

why.text: Margin is guided higher y/y but near the bottom of the target range for the year ex-IEEPA, and Q3 manufacturing costs were unfavorable in each primary segment (Power & Energy on capacity-expansion spend, freight and materials; Construction Industries on freight; Resource Industries on materials including tariffs).

questions_for_management.question: What is the target margin range today, and what drives the move off the bottom in 2027 given capacity costs and tariffs?

why.text: The range is not quantified in the filings, management said it is a progressive target, and it intends to give 2027 detail in January.

questions_for_management.question: How should we read book-to-bill and backlog duration? What share of backlog is hyperscaler or prime-power, and have you seen any slot deferrals or permitting-related changes?

why.text: Book-to-bill slowed to about 1.3, orders are being taken to 2029-2030, and the company declined to quantify hyperscaler share.

questions_for_management.question: What went wrong with the Resource Industries Q3 shipments and commissioning, how much shifts into Q4, and what is the status of the large mining truck ramp and the rail outlook?

why.text: Sales to users were +4%, below expectations, rail retail fell 70% and locomotive deliveries were cut.

questions_for_management.question: Capex was cut to about $3.3B while capacity is expanding. What is deferred or phased, and does it affect the 2030 capacity targets?

why.text: Capex guidance fell from about $3.5B even as Winston-Salem and the $1B Sanford investment were announced.

questions_for_management.question: What is the remaining IEEPA refund exposure on the balance sheet and the likelihood and timing of further recoveries?

why.text: Q3 added $128M after $392M in Q2, the outlook assumes none in Q4, and the 10-Q showed large import-overpayment receivables with uncertain timing.

data_gaps: Whisper EPS and options-implied move are not available yet: no Earnings Whispers preview or live implied move exists before the 2027-01-27 report. The beat/miss record and analyst price-target data from FMP were not available.

The year-earlier base in the XBRL-derived consensus growth figures (+22.7% revenue, +45.1% EPS) is Q3 2025, not Q4 2025. The Q4 2025 base used here is derived from FY2025 less nine-month 2025 and may be affected by share-count rounding; a Q4 2025 release was not read.

A 10/23 article quoted $7.12 EPS (vs $4.95) as 'next quarter' consensus; as it predates the Q3 print it appears to be the Q3 consensus, not Q4. The Q4 consensus used here is M.01's $7.08, and the source's FY EPS figures ($27.74 / $33.46) are pre-Q3.

The Q3 10-Q has not been read; only the 8-K, release and call. Share repurchase authorization remaining, the Q3 ASR status, the IEEPA receivable balance and the 364-day credit facility renewal (due to expire August 2026) are not confirmed.

The target adjusted operating margin range, the MP&E free cash flow target range ($6B-$15B) and the long-term revenue CAGR are not verifiable in the filings. An analyst cited 6%-9% while the 10-K said 5%-7%, and management did not correct it.

The Baird price target of $729 appears inconsistent with other targets ($950-$1,045) and may be a data error; one page also showed CAT -9.25% on the print vs the -3.8% reported elsewhere. Neither is relied on.
The Fabick Cat dealer acquisition (announced Oct 15, outside the 14-day news window) has no terms or Q4 impact in the sources. Any dealer-ownership impact on dealer-inventory dynamics is unknown.
Q4 2025 segment bases and consensus by segment were not available, so segment-level Q4 growth cannot be benchmarked. Peer proxies are dated (Deere's August filing) or distorted by FX (Komatsu's yen).
Long-term debt is not tagged in the Q2 10-Q XBRL, so the long-term debt line is missing from the fact sheet.
